verdict.rationale: ScrapingBee's docs say JavaScript rendering is enabled by default and is useful for single-page applications built with React, Angular or Vue. Its headless browsers can wait for a CSS/XPath selector, or run a JavaScript scenario, before returning the rendered HTML. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that rendered SPA HTML is returned reliably.

support.subject: As a developer, I can render JavaScript-heavy single-page applications and get the fully rendered HTML

citations.quote: JavaScript rendering is enabled by default.
This can be useful for scraping a Single Page Application built with frameworks such as React.js, Angular.js, JQuery or Vue.
Our headless browsers will wait for the CSS / Xpath selector passed in the parameter before returning the HTML.
If you want to interact with pages you want to scrape before we return your the HTML you can add JavaScript scenario to your API call.
